summary: Mode 6 random-look examined part10. Four findings, two substantive. (1) The 'Version History' subsection (p10-3) ends at V4.8 (April 5, 2026) while the review is at V6.0 (package.json version 6.0.0; review-state.json version V6.0; V6 restructure dated 2026-04-07 in CLAUDE.md). Its TLDR claims 'A complete log of substantive changes... Every change is tracked and timestamped' — false by >2 months: missing the V6.0 restructure/renumbering, the progressive-disclosure UX, the predictions scoreboard buildout, and verdict-affecting corrections through June (e.g., the 2026-06-07 Van Camp→Mansinha attribution correction, EXP-603). (2) Worse than stale: the dated V4 entry contains LIVE template variables — 'Updated for V51.0 ({{TOTAL_WINS}} WINs)' renders today as '70 WINs' and '{{NEW_IN_V51}} new WIN reviews' renders '32' — but at V4's own date the correct frozen values were 67 and 28 (V1 entry: 39 V50.6 WINs; 39+28=67; review-state.json records dome's V51.0 arithmetic as 67/(67+4)=95.2%). The historical log entries silently mutate as the catalog grows — mutable history is precisely the failure mode our Timestamp Error analysis criticizes in the dome's OTS practice. (3) 'Key Peer-Reviewed Papers' omits Mansinha, Ducarme, Hinderer, Meurers & van Ruymbeke (2001), now load-bearing after EXP-603 replaced the fabricated Van Camp eclipse attribution with it (5+ inline cites across sections.json). (4) Minor: dataset list says 'IGRF-13' while our own PRED-073 analysis now uses an IGRF-14 extrapolation (commit 2229ba1) and IGRF-14 has been the operative generation since epoch 2025.0; Security Note (p10-4) speaks of V51.0 and the AI Context page in the present tense although the dome is at V51.1 and ai-context has 404'd for weeks (poller baseline), and mentions security-audit.md without hyperlinking it even though the file ships in docs/.
kernel_of_truth: The Version History section was conscientious when written — V4.7's entry even self-corrects ('initially 11 WINs, count has since changed'), showing the drift problem was understood for verdict counts. And using build-time template vars is the right instinct for PRESENT-tense surfaces (the footer's '{{TOTAL_WINS}} claimed wins' is correct usage). The failure is applying a live variable inside a dated changelog entry, where the whole point is immutability. The deeper structural truth: a hand-maintained changelog will ALWAYS go stale under a daily agent pipeline that lands multiple substantive commits per week — the durable fix is to scope the section to major milestones and delegate the 'complete log' claim to the public git history, which actually IS complete and timestamped.
